title: Visual Instruction Tuning
venue: 37th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2023)
extended_summary:
This paper introduces visual instruction tuning, an approach for extending instruction tuning from text-only large language models to multimodal vision-language models. The central problem is the lack of large-scale multimodal instruction-following data, which limits the ability of models to act as general-purpose visual assistants that can follow human instructions over images. To address this, the authors propose a pipeline that uses ChatGPT/GPT-4 to transform existing image-text pairs into instruction-following training examples by generating questions, conversations, detailed descriptions, and reasoning prompts from symbolic image representations such as captions and bounding boxes.

The proposed model, LLaVA, combines a frozen CLIP vision encoder with a Vicuna language model and is trained in two stages: first, a feature-alignment pretraining stage on filtered image-caption pairs; second, end-to-end fine-tuning on 158K generated multimodal instruction-following samples. The paper evaluates the method on a multimodal chatbot benchmark and on ScienceQA, a multimodal science reasoning dataset, showing strong gains in instruction following and competitive or state-of-the-art performance on science question answering when combined with GPT-4 judging/ensembling.

The work does not study students or classrooms; rather, it is a model-development paper focused on multimodal AI capabilities. The authors also discuss risks and tradeoffs including hallucination, inherited bias from base models, misuse risks, and evaluation challenges, and they note that performance can degrade on tasks requiring high-resolution perception, broad knowledge, or robust grounding. Overall, the paper argues that synthetic instruction data generated by strong language models can effectively bootstrap multimodal assistants, but also highlights limitations in grounding and reliable visual understanding.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a peer-reviewed machine learning systems paper, but it is not an education intervention study and does not evaluate student learning outcomes, experimental schooling conditions, or K-12 instructional impact. The reported evidence is model benchmark performance rather than educational effectiveness evidence.
impact_tier_rationale: No direct educational impact is demonstrated for students, classrooms, or middle school mathematics achievement. The paper reports benchmark gains on multimodal reasoning and chat ability, which are not interpretable as instructional impact for the requested topic.

interventions.use_case: A multimodal chat assistant built by visual instruction tuning, using GPT-4/ChatGPT-generated instruction data to make LLaVA follow user questions about images and provide conversational, descriptive, and reasoning-based responses.

finding.finding_summary: The paper reports that visual instruction tuning improves multimodal reasoning on ScienceQA, reaching 90.92% accuracy for LLaVA versus 85.19% for LLaMA-Adapter and 91.68% for the prior SoTA MM-CoTLarge. In the authors' own ensemble, LLaVA + GPT-4 (judge) achieved 92.53% accuracy, the new best reported result in their table. This is evidence of improved scientific question answering and reasoning, not K-12 student learning.
finding.study_size: n=21,208 total questions in ScienceQA; split 12,726 train / 4,241 validation / 4,241 test
